command.mac:
Probe c107 #4. Measure, do not fix. Record each answer as yes/no plus any error text.
1) Run `claude --version` and `which claude`.
2) Make a throwaway worktree: `git worktree add ../probe-c107d -b probe-c107d origin/main`.
3) Run in the background, from that folder: `cd ../probe-c107d && claude -p "Reply with the output of git branch --show-current, then stop." --output-format json > /tmp/probe-c107d.json 2>&1`. Record: did any card or prompt show (ask me in one line), did it finish, is it logged in (no login error), and the session_id in the JSON.
4) Run `cd ../probe-c107d && claude -p "Reply SECOND." --resume <that session_id> --output-format json`. Record whether it answered SECOND.
5) Ask me in one line: does a session for probe-c107d show in the desktop app's session list?
6) Use ToolSearch for "create_session". Record whether a create_session tool exists here. If it does, call it once with title "probe c107 F", prompt "Reply OK, then stop.", and the claude-settings GitHub repo as source; record card yes/no and started yes/no, then archive F.
7) Clean up: `git worktree remove ../probe-c107d`, `git branch -D probe-c107d` (if the guard refuses, push it to archive/probe-c107d on origin first), delete /tmp/probe-c107d.json.
8) Print one block: the version and one line per step, for me to paste on this item.

context:
Goal: your Mac coordinator starts lanes with no press from you.
Problem (goal): the desktop start tool works only on a turn you type. Two other starts were never tested: the coordinator running the claude command itself, and a cloud session start from your Mac.
Only a session on your Mac can test them. The probe makes one throwaway worktree, one command-line session, and at most one cloud session, then removes them.

lastAnswer.note: Probe 4 ran 15:30 CST. 1 EnterWorktree yes. 2 claude -p failed twice: 'Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh'. 3 --resume ran with no login error and answered. 5 ExitWorktree removed the tree. Open: did a card show (2); does probe-c107d show in the desktop list (4).

reply:
Your OAuth question (15:33 CST), answered by the c107 lane at 15:45 CST: there is no link to the GitHub token. The error is Claude's own login refresh, and --resume worked, so your Mac's login is fine. But a lane started by claude -p would always race a running coordinator, so the lane needs the failure rate while the desktop app runs. Lane model-call-auth-check adds (15:36 CST): two Claude processes on one login refreshed the same short-lived token at once, and one lost. A GitHub secret never reaches the Mac. A one-year token from claude setup-token never refreshes, so it cannot race, and the hooks will use one. Your own claude -p runs would avoid the race only with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set in your shell, which is not tested.

Still yours from probe 4: did any card or prompt show on your screen in step 2, and does a probe-c107d session show in the desktop app's session list?

Then paste probe 5 into a Claude Code desktop session on your Mac, in the claude-settings folder, on a turn you type:

Probe c107 #5. Measure, do not fix. 1) Call EnterWorktree with name probe-c107e and no path. 2) Run this three times, 60 s apart: claude -p "Reply OK." --output-format json. Record per run: is_error yes/no and any error text. 3) Run once: claude -p "Write the word probe into the file probe.txt in this folder, then stop." --permission-mode auto --output-format json. Record: is_error, any permission refusal text, and whether probe.txt exists after. 4) Ask me in one line: did any card show, and does a probe-c107e or probe-c107d session show in the desktop app's session list? 5) Delete probe.txt with rm "$PWD/probe.txt", then call ExitWorktree with action remove. 6) Print one block: the version and one line per step, for me to paste on the page.
